_comment: Live pages the downloadWebPage tool must keep reading correctly. Markers are strings that MUST appear in the extracted markdown ('expect') or MUST NOT ('reject'). Ratios are not asserted: the counter-tariff page scored a healthy-looking 0.711 text-coverage while serving an entirely superseded list, so only named content proves the right part of the page was read. Cites = times the page was cited in production over one month, where known.

pages.why: Most-cited page in production. Readability returned a 138-token sidebar blurb and dropped the H1 and the whole funding-programs list.
Three dated lists in sibling <details>. The tool served only the superseded 2025 list, unlabelled, and reported success.
expect: Complete list of U.S. products subject to counter tariffs
pages.note: 0402.10.10 is the first item of the September 8, 2026 list; 0105.11.22 belongs to the superseded list that used to crowd it out. The page exceeds the token cap, so a [TRUNCATED] notice is expected and correct.

pages.why: 34 accordions; roughly two-thirds of the page was being discarded.
Extraction began mid-page at 'Worker supports', losing the title and the Rapid Response Supports intro.
expect: Support for workers impacted by tariffs

pages.why: 13 accordions; three-quarters of the page discarded.
Readability dropped the H1 and the entire 'Most requested' top-task list.
14 accordions; retained 1.6% of <main>. Highest-loss page found in the scenario corpus.
Healthy page — guards against the <main> path regressing a page Readability already handled well.
Healthy page with accordions — guards against regression.

unreadable.why: JavaScript-rendered; the body says only 'Loading'. The tool correctly refuses it, but the agent cites it anyway. Not fixed by extraction.
Returns breadcrumbs only and passes MIN_CONTENT_CHARS, so it reports success on a page it did not really read. Not fixed by extraction.
